Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 94, verse 1:

These verses show that there was some constriction in the soul of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and that he felt certain difficulties in connection with the call to Islam. He was distressed, because plots were being hatched against him and their effects were falling upon his heart, and he felt that these responsibilities were very heavy and that he needed the help, support and special provision of Allah.

Accordingly, this dialogue took place on that occasion. The manner of speech is such that the words are filled with affection.

﴿Alam nashrah laka sadrak﴾ (1:94) "(O Prophet), did We not open your chest for you?" Your chest was opened for the work of the call to Islam, and We made the bearing of this responsibility easy for you. We made this responsibility beloved to you, cleared the path, and set you upon that very path, until its outcome became clearly visible to you, full of felicities.

Just feel your own chest: do you not find in it expansiveness, joy and a radiance? Do you not clearly find the taste of this religion of Allah? Tell us, truly: in every difficulty and hardship, do you not find this? In every fatigue, do you not feel joy? Does every hardship not seem easy to you? Are you not content with every deprivation?

"And We removed from you your burden, which had weighed down your back" (94:2–3).

That is, the burden of the Islamic call had become so heavy that it was close to breaking your back. We bestowed upon you expansion of the breast, and this burden became light. We granted you the ability to carry out the work, made the task of calling to the Faith easy for you, and it began to reach the hearts of people. The flow of revelation continued, and through revelation realities began to be unveiled. And thus this call began to settle into hearts. Through revelation, this work began to proceed with great ease, gentleness and tranquility. Do you not perceive this change in that burden which had broken your back, and which has now become light? After the expansion of your breast, there is now neither burden upon you nor constriction of the heart.

"And We raised high your remembrance for you" (94:4). Your mention was lifted up in the higher realm; the call of your mission resounded across the whole earth; your name was exalted throughout this entire universe, and then your name was joined with the name of Allah in the kalimah tayyibah.

La ilaha illa Allah, Muhammad Rasul Allah: whenever anyone recites this kalimah, your name will be exalted. What higher station could there be after this? This is a unique status of yours, reserved for you alone among all creatures.

We placed your mention in the Preserved Tablet (Lawh Mahfuz), so that ages would pass, generations would come and go, and millions of lips would continue to utter your blessed name, sending salutations and peace upon you, and expressing deep love, reverence and honour for you. Your remembrance was also raised in this way: your name became bound up with the Islamic system of life and the Shariah of Muhammad. It was your selection alone that became the cause of the elevation of your remembrance. This is a station that no one has ever attained, nor ever will. Therefore, where is hardship now, and where is weariness? This religion is so great that in its presence the sense of every kind of hardship and fatigue simply disappears.

Yet despite all this, Allah bestows further kindnesses upon His beloved, the chosen one: He removes your distresses even further, makes you happy and content, and gives you the news that great ease and abundance await you.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 94, verses 5–6:

"So indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease."

The truth is that with hardship there is necessarily ease, and after hardship there come ease and facilities. And O Prophet, this has always remained with you as well. When the burden of the call became heavy upon you, We opened your heart, and thus your burden was lightened, the burden which had broken your back. Therefore, alongside hardship, ease remained attached, and this heavy burden became light.

This is an unchanging principle, and therefore it has been repeated in the very same words.

"Fa inna ma'al-'usri... yusra" (94:6): "So indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease." This repetition expresses that at the time these verses were being revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in extreme hardship and difficulty. Therefore Allah addressed this matter in this manner, reminding him, and He mentioned His previous favours upon the person of the Prophet (ﷺ), spoke of His grace, kindness and support, and further emphasised the same principle for the future, so that you would be consoled that a better era is coming. It appears from this that the difficulties in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was surrounded were severe difficulties.

Now it is explained how the better era that is coming to you will arrive, what the true causes of the expansion of the breast (inshirah al-sadr) are, and what provision is for the long path of the Islamic call and the arduous journey, and what the means of being quenched are.

Verily, with hardship comes ease; indeed, with hardship comes ease. And these are its means: act upon them. When you have finished with your occupations with people and with the affairs of this world, and the activities of life have come to a measure of rest, then once you are free of these matters, move into the field where effort and striving are needed, namely the worship of Allah and turning your attention to Allah.

﴿And turn eagerly to your Lord﴾ (94:8). So turn only to your Lord, leave aside all worldly affairs, even leaving aside the activities of the Islamic call (da'wah). This is the provision for the journey. Every journey requires some equipment, and this is the equipment for this journey. Jihad requires preparation, and this is the preparation; and as a result, ease will come in place of hardship. Spaciousness will come in difficulty, and this is indeed the correct method.

The conclusion of this surah is similar to that of Surah al-Duha. At its close, two kinds of feelings settle in the heart. One is that Allah has an extraordinarily great love for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and fresh breezes of this love keep coming from the higher realm moment by moment. The second is that, alongside this love, the Divine Being has boundless compassion and sympathy for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). And from both surahs it is felt that at that time the Messenger (ﷺ) was passing through a very difficult period. Therefore there was a need for the expression of this love and compassion from the higher realm. This is the heavy responsibility of the call to the truth; it is back-breaking, but upon those who carry out this task, the light and mercy of Allah remain ever vigilant.
